The '''1963–64 [[Serie A]]''' season was won by [[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]].

==Teams==
[[A.C.R. Messina|Messina]], [[AS Bari|Bari]] and [[SS Lazio|Lazio]] had been promoted from [[Serie B]].

==Championship tie-breaker==
With both Inter and Bologna level on 54 points, a play-off match was conducted to decide the champion for the first and only time in Serie A history.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Dream_Cup/Primo_Piano/2007/07_Luglio/Bologna_64.shtml|title=Il Bologna di Bernardini e lo storico spareggio|publisher=gazzetta.it|language=Italian}}</ref>
{{football box
|date=7 June 1964
|time=
|team1=[[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]]
|score=2–0
|aet=
|report=
|team2=[[Inter Milan|Internazionale]]
|goals1=[[Giacinto Facchetti|Facchetti]] {{goal|75|o.g.}}<br />[[Harald Nielsen|Nielsen]] {{goal|82}}
|goals2=
|stadium=[[Stadio Olimpico]], [[Rome]]
|attendance=
|referee=[[Concetto Lo Bello]]
}}
